Print a ledger of dated entries as a fixed-width table, with dates and amounts in American or Dutch style.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/ledger) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: ledger.nomi
//# Prints a ledger of dated entries as a table, in American or Dutch style.

import {
    std/calendar.{Date, DateFields}
    std/currency.Currency
    std/locale.Locale
    std/money.{CurrencySign, Money}
}

/// One line of the ledger: when, what for, and the change in cents, negative
/// for money spent.
pub struct Entry {
    date: Date
    description: String
    cents: Int
}

/// The two styles the ledger is printed in: their headings, dates and amounts.
pub enum Style {
    American
    Dutch
}

impl Style {
    fn locale(style: Style) -> Locale {
        case style {
            .American -> Locale`en-US`
            .Dutch -> Locale`nl-NL`
        }
    }

    /// How the style writes a negative amount: American style as an
    /// accountant does, in parentheses.
    fn sign(style: Style) -> CurrencySign {
        case style {
            .American -> CurrencySign.Accounting
            .Dutch -> CurrencySign.Standard
        }
    }

    fn headings(style: Style) -> #(String, String, String) {
        case style {
            .American -> #("Date", "Description", "Change")
            .Dutch -> #("Datum", "Omschrijving", "Verandering")
        }
    }
}

/// The ledger's lines: a heading, then each entry by date, description and
/// change, with amounts in `currency` written in `style`.
pub fn format_entries(currency: Currency, style: Style, entries: List<Entry>) -> List<String> {
    #(date, description, change) = Style.headings(style)
    heading = row(date, description, String.pad_end(change, 13))

    lines =
        entries
        |> Iter.sort_by(fn entry -> #(entry.date, entry.description, entry.cents))
        |> Iter.map(&format_entry(currency, style, &1))

    [heading, ..lines]
}

fn format_entry(currency: Currency, style: Style, entry: Entry) -> String {
    locale = Style.locale(style)
    date = Date.format_fields(entry.date, locale, DateFields`yMMdd`)
    change = #Money{amount: Int.to_decimal(entry.cents) * 0.01d, currency}
    row(date, truncate(entry.description), format_change(change, style))
}

/// The table's three columns: a date ten wide, a description 25 wide, and
/// a change 13 wide, right-aligned. The heading pads its change on the
/// right first, so its title is left-aligned.
fn row(date: String, description: String, change: String) -> String {
    [String.pad_end(date, 10), String.pad_end(description, 25), String.pad_start(change, 13)]
    |> String.join(" | ")
}

/// `description` cut to 22 characters and an ellipsis when it is wider than
/// its column.
fn truncate(description: String) -> String {
    if String.length(description) <= 25 {
        description
    } else {
        String.take(description, 22) + "..."
    }
}

/// An amount as the style writes it. An amount not in parentheses ends with
/// a space, so the digits line up with the parenthesized ones.
fn format_change(change: Money, style: Style) -> String {
    amount =
        Money.format(change, Style.locale(style), display: .Narrow, sign: Style.sign(style))
        |> String.replace("\u{a0}", " ")

    if String.ends_with(amount, ")") {
        amount
    } else {
        "${amount} "
    }
}

// FILE: ledger_test.nomi
import {
    std/calendar.Date
    std/currency.Currency
    ledger.{self, Entry, Style}
}

test "ledger" {
    cases: List<#(String, Currency, Style, List<Entry>, List<String>)> = [
        #(
            "empty ledger",
            Currency`USD`,
            Style.American,
            [],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "one entry",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Buy present", cents: -1000},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Buy present               |      ($10.00)",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "credit and debit",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-01-02`, description: "Get present", cents: 1000},
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Buy present", cents: -1000},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Buy present               |      ($10.00)",
                "01/02/2015 | Get present               |       $10.00 ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "multiple entries on same date ordered by description, as first written",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-01-02`, description: "Get present", cents: 1000},
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Buy present", cents: -1000},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Buy present               |      ($10.00)",
                "01/02/2015 | Get present               |       $10.00 ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "final order tie breaker is change",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Something", cents: 0},
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Something", cents: -1},
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Something", cents: 1},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Something                 |       ($0.01)",
                "01/01/2015 | Something                 |        $0.00 ",
                "01/01/2015 | Something                 |        $0.01 ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "overlong description is truncated",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{
                    date: Date`2015-01-01`,
                    description: "Freude schoner Gotterfunken",
                    cents: -123456,
                },
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Freude schoner Gotterf... |   ($1,234.56)",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "euros",
            Currency`EUR`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Buy present", cents: -1000},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Buy present               |      (€10.00)",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "Dutch locale",
            Currency`USD`,
            .Dutch,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-03-12`, description: "Buy present", cents: 123456},
            ],
            [
                "Datum      | Omschrijving              | Verandering  ",
                "12-03-2015 | Buy present               |   $ 1.234,56 ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "Dutch locale and euros",
            Currency`EUR`,
            .Dutch,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-03-12`, description: "Buy present", cents: 123456},
            ],
            [
                "Datum      | Omschrijving              | Verandering  ",
                "12-03-2015 | Buy present               |   € 1.234,56 ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "Dutch negative number with 3 digits before decimal point",
            Currency`USD`,
            .Dutch,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-03-12`, description: "Buy present", cents: -12345},
            ],
            [
                "Datum      | Omschrijving              | Verandering  ",
                "12-03-2015 | Buy present               |    $ -123,45 ",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "American negative number with 3 digits before decimal point",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-03-12`, description: "Buy present", cents: -12345},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "03/12/2015 | Buy present               |     ($123.45)",
            ],
        ),
        #(
            "multiple entries on same date ordered by description",
            Currency`USD`,
            .American,
            [
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Get present", cents: 1000},
                #{date: Date`2015-01-01`, description: "Buy present", cents: -1000},
            ],
            [
                "Date       | Description               | Change       ",
                "01/01/2015 | Buy present               |      ($10.00)",
                "01/01/2015 | Get present               |       $10.00 ",
            ],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, currency, style, entries, expected), description {
        assert ledger.format_entries(currency, style, entries) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The exercise is a refactoring one: tracks ship a badly written printer to clean up. There is no Nomi stub to start from, so this is the solution written directly, against the canonical cases.
- The canonical `locale` input, `en_US` or `nl_NL`, is a `Style` enum, `American` or `Dutch`, since the ledger has headings for those two and no others. Each style knows its std `Locale` and its three headings.
- Dates and amounts come from std's CLDR data rather than hand-written patterns. `Date.format_fields` with the skeleton `yMMdd` writes `01/01/2015` in `en-US` and `12-03-2015` in `nl-NL`, and `Money.format` with the `Narrow` symbol writes `$1,234.56` and `$ 1.234,56` (US dollars are `US$` in Dutch with the plain symbol).
- An American negative amount is in parentheses, `($10.00)`, which is CLDR's accounting pattern for `en`: `Money.format` with `sign: .Accounting` writes it, and `Style.sign` picks it for American style only, since the canonical Dutch lines write `$ -123,45`.
- One thing is the ledger's own and is done by hand: the Dutch amount's no-break space after the symbol becomes a plain space, which the canonical lines use.
- An entry holds its change in cents, as the canonical input does, and the currency is the ledger's. The change becomes a `Money` only to be formatted.
- The entries are sorted by one tuple key, `#(date, description, cents)` (style §32).
- A row is its three columns padded and joined with `" | "`. The heading pads its last title on the right before the row pads it on the left, so the title sits at the left of its column and the amounts at the right.
- The twelve canonical cases are one `subtests` table. Two canonical cases share the description "multiple entries on same date ordered by description"; the first of them, whose entries are on different dates, is named "..., as first written" so each row has its own name.
